stem: The table shows values of f(x) for x near 2: f(1.9)=5.9, f(1.99)=5.99, f(1.999)=5.999, f(2.001)=6.001, f(2.01)=6.01, f(2.1)=6.1. Based on the table, what is lim(x->2) f(x)?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Does not exist, since the left- and right-side values are never exactly equal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cannot be determined without knowing f(2)

rationales.A: Approaching, not equaling, is what matters for a limit.
rationales.B: Reads a single table entry instead of the trend.
rationales.D: A limit does not require the function value at the point.

stem:
What is lim(x→∞) (5x²−x+4)/(2x²+3)?
No calculator is permitted.

rationales.A: Incorrectly applies the rule for a lower-degree numerator.
rationales.B: Reverses the ratio of the leading coefficients.
rationales.C: Uses the denominator's degree as the limit.

stem:
Let f(x)=kx+1 for x<2 and f(x)=x²−1 for x≥2. For what value of k is f continuous at x=2?
No calculator is permitted.

rationales.A: Sets the left-hand expression equal to 1 instead of the function value at 2.
rationales.B: Correctly equates the one-sided limit and function value.
rationales.C: Divides the right-side value by 2 without subtracting 1.
rationales.D: Uses the input value as the parameter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Does not exist, because the denominator equals 0 at x = -2

rationales.A: Arithmetic slip: evaluates x+3 at x=2 instead of x=-2.
rationales.B: Plugs x=-2 into the numerator alone and stops before simplifying.
rationales.C: Cancel the common factor, then evaluate x+3 at x=-2.
rationales.D: Misses that it is a removable discontinuity, not a true division by zero.

stem: The tangent line to y=ln x at x=e is

rationales.A: The point is (e,1) and the slope is 1/e.
rationales.C: This uses slope e instead of 1/e.
rationales.D: This omits the y-coordinate 1 of the tangency point.

stem:
What is d/dx[sec x tan x]?
No calculator is permitted.

rationales.A: Combines derivative pieces but omits one tangent factor.
rationales.B: Subtracts the product-rule terms instead of adding.
rationales.C: Correctly applies the product rule to both trigonometric factors.
rationales.D: Uses tangent rather than secant as the common factor.

stem:
Which expression equals f′(3)?
No calculator is permitted.

rationales.A: Correctly instantiates the derivative definition at x=3.
rationales.B: Uses inconsistent base inputs and divides by the fixed point.
rationales.C: Divides by the point rather than the input change.
rationales.D: Keeps a fixed denominator instead of the increment.

stem:
Which statement is always true?
No calculator is permitted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A function with a derivative of 0 at x=a has a local extremum there.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A function can be differentiable where it is discontinuous.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a function is differentiable at x=a, then it is continuous there.

rationales.A: A corner can be continuous but not differentiable.
rationales.B: A horizontal tangent need not be an extremum.
rationales.C: Differentiability cannot occur at a discontinuity.

rationales.B: The product rule and chain rule give 2e^(2x)sin x+e^(2x)cos x.
rationales.C: The factors of 2 are attached to the wrong term.
rationales.D: This differentiates e^(2x) incorrectly and omits a product-rule term.

rationales.A: Applying the chain rule to (1+x³)^(1/2) gives 3x²/(2√(1+x³)).
rationales.B: The derivative of the outer square root is inverted.
rationales.D: The derivative of x³ is not 3x.

stem:
For the curve x²+y²=25, what is dy/dx at (3,4)?
No calculator is permitted.

rationales.A: Uses the negative reciprocal of the correct slope.
rationales.D: Interchanges x and y and drops the sign.

stem: On x²+xy+y²=7, what is dy/dx at (1,2)?

rationales.A: This takes the negative reciprocal of the correct slope.
rationales.B: Implicit differentiation gives 2x+y+(x+2y)y′=0, so y′=−4/5 at (1,2).
rationales.C: The sign from moving 2x+y is missing.
rationales.D: Both sign and reciprocal are incorrect.
